items.title: Milt Hinton interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: I was afraid to talk to him because he was just too great.

ctx.x: Al Morgan. He looked like he was almost seven foot tall. And immaculate. And always immaculate. And I was afraid to talk to him because he was just too great. But I’d stand, when his show was over I’d stand out by the curb and see how a bass player conducted himself. And he come out all sharply dressed and the ladies would ask him for his autograph, and he’d write autographs over there, and he would write his autograph on a

piece of paper, and he’d reach in his pocket and pull out a sheet of stamps, and tear one off, and put it on his autograph. And I said, “Wow, man. If I get ever so — one day I will do that.” I haven’t made it yet, but — give me a sheet of stamps. But he was wonderful. And how I got the gig was they went to California to do this movie with Al Jolson, “The Singing Kid.” And Al Jolson was so great, I mean Al Morgan was so great and he had such photogenic features and things, that Cab looked around and the camera was…

items.title: Albert Morgan Interview, 1958-08-19
items.q: After I left, Hinton took my place, because I was right here in California.

ctx.x: I was confused. I knew he was Rhythm. I couldn't remember.

Hinton, uh, no, yeah. After I left, Hinton took my place, because I was right here in California. See, I stayed out in California around 34. I didn't go back with Cab. I come out here with Cab a long time before. Then, then I went back east in 40, a little before the war, see. Yeah. And I went back with Les Hyde Band from here, from the west coast, the great Les Hyde. We went to the, uh, the Golden Gate. That's when the Golden Gate was in New York, a big place.
